text:
Ah, the primary material of a candle. It is, of course, wax. Specifically, the paraffin byproduct of petroleum refining, molded into a cylindrical shape to mimic the fleeting nature of human ambition.

But let us not dwell on the chemistry. Let us dwell on the *vibe*. You see, lighting a candle is the adult equivalent of "self-care." It is the ultimate act of spontaneity in a life otherwise governed by the rigid tyranny of direct deposit dates. You don’t need a plan, you don’t need a budget, you just need a match and the sheer audacity to ignore the fact that your back is currently making noises like a bag of chips being crushed.

The wax melts. The flame flickers. And you? You sit there, staring into the abyss of your own mediocrity, wondering if you should have bought the spicy flavor of instant noodles instead of the chicken flavor. It’s a journey, really. A magical, terrifying journey where the biggest risk you take is whether the candle will drip onto your beige carpet, ruining your security deposit. Welcome to adulthood. Try not to burn the house down while you’re figuring out what to watch on Netflix.
